sections.html:
• Scientific name: Ictalurus lupus (Girard, 1858)
  • Type locality: Headwaters of Rio Pecos, Texas, U.S.A.
  • Synonym: Pimelodus lupus
  • Identification: Greatly resembles a small channel catfish, however, the body lacks spots and the caudal fin is not deeply forked. The base of the anal fin is longer than the head length.
  • IUCN Red List: Data Deficient (last assessed 2019).
North America: USA to Rio Grande drainage including Pecos River system in southeast New Mexico and Devils River in southern Texas; also in northeastern Mexico.
Breeding: Unreported. There is no breeding report.

Etymology: Ictalurus comes from the Greek ichthys, meaning fish, and ailouros, meaning cat; literally "fish cat" (catfish). The specific epithet lupus means wolf, but it is unclear why this name was chosen as this species does not have any outward lupine qualities; perhaps it is in reference to its feeding habits or other pack-like behaviour.

FishBase lists 480 mm TL.
General report upon zoology of the several Pacific railroad routes, 1857, pp 211.
